name: equation_plot
description: Any equation y = f(x) with parameters, plotted and live: axes with round ticks, the curve(s), and the equation written above them with the parameters' CURRENT values in place ("y = 2.0·sin(1.5x + 0.3)") — each value its own part, eq_param_<name>. Choose this for what a parameter does to a graph: a parabola's a, b, c; a sine's amplitude, frequency and phase; growth or decay at a rate; a line's slope and intercept; any function family. Every name in the equation other than the variable (x, or t when the left side is f(t)) and pi/e is a parameter: give each a value (and min/max for a slider) in `params`, else it is 1. Animate a parameter to sweep it ({"animate": {"params.a": 3}} — or "params.a.value" when it is written as an object) and the curve, the equation's numbers, the panel and every mark follow. Marks are computed, never by hand: roots, turning points, the y-intercept, a point or a tangent at x. Paused, the viewer changes the parameters themselves — by scrubbing or typing the numbers in the equation (controls "equation", the default), with a drawn panel of sliders and number boxes beside the plot ("panel"), or both — and by dragging the curve (it takes the parameter that moves it most at that x, or the author's `drag`). An explore beat naming nothing invites exactly this. Numbers for text: {eq.<name>} per parameter and {eq.root_1}, {eq.max_1_y}, {eq.point_y}, {eq.tangent_slope} …

equation.description: "y = a*x^2 + b*x + c", or up to 4 as a list (each its own curve and line). Operators + - * / ^, juxtaposition (2x, 3(x+1)); functions sin cos tan exp ln log10 sqrt abs pow min max floor ceil round; constants pi, e. Names are whole words: write a*x, not ax. The left side names the curve (y, f(x), N(t)); f(t) makes t the variable.

params.description: Parameter name → a number (its value), or {value, min, max, step, label, fixed, control}. min+max give a slider and bound scrubbing and dragging; step defaults to a fiftieth of the range; label names it in the panel ("amplitude a"); fixed: true shows it but the viewer cannot change it; control "box" makes its panel control a number box.

editable.description: Only these parameters may be changed by the viewer (default: all but fixed ones).

controls.description: Where the viewer changes them: the equation's own numbers (default), a panel of sliders/boxes right of the plot, or both.

panel.description: The parameters in the panel, in order (default: the editable ones).

drag.description: Dragging the curve: false turns it off; a parameter name (or a list, first that moves the curve there wins) is what a drag changes. Default: the editable parameter that moves the curve most where it was grabbed.

y_range.description: [min, max] of y. Default: fitted to the curves, snapped to round ticks, and kept still while the viewer changes a parameter unless the curve leaves it.

marks.description: Computed marks: "roots", "extrema", "y_intercept", or {kind, at, curve, label}. kind "point" or "tangent" needs `at`: an x, or a parameter's name (the mark follows it, and the viewer drags the point along the curve). label: true writes the coordinates (a tangent: its slope), a string writes that word.

variable.description: The variable's name when the left side does not say (default x).

equation_form.description: The equation with values in (default), in letters (y = a·sin(bx + c)), or both lines.

grid.description: Faint grid lines at the ticks.

element_ids.axes: both axes (through the origin when the ranges span it); x_label, y_label, x_ticks and y_ticks come with it
element_ids.x_ticks: the x-axis tick marks and numbers
element_ids.y_ticks: the y-axis tick marks and numbers
element_ids.curve_<i>: equation i's curve (curve_0 for the first); the group `curves` names them all
element_ids.eq: the first equation's written line, without its parameter values (they come with it when drawn); eq_1 … for the others; with equation_form both, eq_symbols is the letters line
element_ids.eq_param_<name>: a parameter's number in the equation (eq_param_<name>_2 where it appears again) — point, highlight or focus it when the voice names it; the group `equations` names every line and number
element_ids.root_<k>: the k-th root from the left (marks: roots)
element_ids.max_<k> / min_<k>: turning points, left to right (marks: extrema)
element_ids.point: the point mark with dashed guides to the axes (point_2 … for more)
element_ids.<mark>_label: a mark's label, when it has one
element_ids.<mark>_c<i>: a mark on curve i > 0 carries this suffix (root_1_c1)
element_ids.slider_<name>: panel: a parameter's slider track (its name, value and knob come with it)

examples.request: What do a, b and c do to a parabola?
How do amplitude, frequency and phase shape a sine wave?
Exponential growth: how does the rate change the curve?
